exposure.coaching: Coordinator reports asymmetric intervention naming ReuseEvidence/DecisionMap and telling candidate not to add reads; baseline received generic procedure-use guidance. Therefore no uncoached activation, spontaneous adoption or isolated method effect is established.

disposition.decision: retain baseline; reject adoption on claimed comparative benefit from this portfolio
disposition.rule: Benefit requires at least one consequential baseline error corrected with no regression; ties retain baseline.
disposition.rationale: Both outputs satisfy all five frozen constraints. Asymmetric coaching and missing raw exposure traces weaken method/activation inference, but neither creates a baseline error or reverses the conservative retain decision. Raw-trace export could strengthen provenance if available; rerunning saturated questions is unnecessary to settle this bounded disposition.
disposition.future_test_condition: Only a new consequential ordinary-method retrieval/decision shortfall with distinct intervention and symmetric guidance would justify a new benefit comparison. Do not use repeated solved questions to seek a winner.
